title: Evaluating cos^2(pi/8) via the Half-Angle Formula
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Use a half-angle identity to find the exact value of \cos^2(\pi/8).

steps.title: State the Half-Angle Formula for Cosine Squared
steps.explanation: Recall the half-angle (power-reducing) identity cos^2(theta) = (1 + cos(2*theta))/2.
steps.why: Rearranging the double-angle identity cos(2*theta) = 2*cos^2(theta) - 1 gives cos^2(theta) = (1 + cos(2*theta))/2.

steps.title: Substitute theta = pi/8
steps.explanation: Set theta = pi/8 so that 2*theta = pi/4.
steps.why: Doubling pi/8 produces the standard 45-degree angle pi/4.

steps.title: Evaluate cos(pi/4) and Simplify the Complex Fraction
steps.explanation: Substitute cos(pi/4) = sqrt(2)/2 and multiply numerator and denominator by 2.
steps.why: Clearing the inner denominator 2 yields (2 + sqrt(2))/4.
